doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

chapter: Michael, influences and the Brecker Brothers
title: Blindfold-style test, 'Slick Stuff' and the end of Dreams
summary: Rowe plays 'Slick Stuff'; Brecker explains Dreams ended when Billy Cobham joined Mahavishnu, prompting a three-horn project.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So you’re probably familiar with the DownBeat blindfold tests.
Yeah so I’m going to play a tune for you if you don’t mind.

Okay. I only heard a little thing. Well that was the general writing style, you know, my style at that point in time where we had had some success with one single that sold a lot called “Sneaking Up Behind You” on the first record, the first Brecker Brother record. Now I have to preface that, and I’ve told the story many times but I might as well recount it here. I had at one point in my life, and this was after joining Horace and I think it was — let me think for a second here — yeah it was after joining Horace we formed a band called Dreams and Mahavishnu came along and they got Billy Cobham from our band.
